FEATURE ("evidence append", approved by Brandon). When the engine resolves a scene-local bare noun to exactly one thing (resolve_references in storygame/runtime/reference_resolution.py returns ReferenceResult.resolutions = ((noun, entity_id), ...) with question None), append the resolved thing's full display name to the text that the EXACT/SHADOW evidence matchers see, and nothing else. Today the command passes through unchanged, so e.g. 'Copy the encrypted Project Echelon file to my laptop.' earns nothing in scene 2C although 'file' resolves uniquely to 'copied JANUS files'. Measured offline over 250 recorded commands (.plans/stage4-reference-sim-2026-10-16.md, script scripts/ringer/stage4/reference_sim.py): exactly 3 commands change: 2C 'Copy the encrypted Project Echelon file to my laptop.' gains k_sl_2c_c_r1; 3A 'Lead the captives through the emergency gate.' and 'Guide the captives through the open emergency gate.' gain k_sl_3a_c_r1.

WHERE. CloudflareTurnProvider._evidence_input (storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py ~line 449) already appends the recent-cue owner name. Extend it: compute the resolution names from the provider's current state with resolve_references(self.state, player_input) (pure function, no state change; for an answered/capped clarification the engine has already spliced the full name into player_input so resolutions come back empty there, which is fine). Add a small public helper in reference_resolution.py, e.g. resolved_reference_names(state, command) -> tuple[str, ...], returning the display names (use the same display_name/world_for path the module already uses) of uniquely resolved things, in order, deduplicated, skipping any name already present in the command (case-insensitive whole-phrase). In _evidence_input append them, then the recent-cue owner (skip the owner if it is already among the appended names), separated by single spaces. Record the appended names in self.last_reveal_selection['reference_names'] (list, empty when none) next to the existing 'recent_cue_owner'.

HARD RULES. The narrator prompt context['player_input'], the negation check and the semantic matcher keep the ORIGINAL player_input; only the exact/shadow evidence input changes (same boundary as the recent cue). Appending names must never create a reveal alone: do not touch eligibility, requires or selection logic. No new persisted state. Do not change ClarificationTurn handling or the engine.

In scene 2C at the right point, 'Copy the encrypted Project Echelon file to my laptop.' earns k_sl_2c_c_r1 (find the setup the real chain needs by reading the 2C knowledge entries; the prerequisite facts may need to be asserted); a control proving it did NOT earn it before the change is the git stash check below.
